items.title: The Ghost of the Native Speaker and the Dark Energy Shadowing the Learner: A Posthumanist Inquiry into Human– AI Relationships in Second Language Writing
items.abstract: Abstract While existing research indicates the utility of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) in assisting language learners, how human–AI relationships may condition learners' being and becoming remains underexplored. In this article, we draw on Barad's agential realism to discuss findings of a posthumanist phenomenological study on 110 Chinese students' experiences with GenAI in a L2 writing workshop. Five forms of human–AI relationships are identified from the metaphors that the student participants employed to describe their experiences: user–tool, king–minister, friend–partner, student–teacher, and slave–tyrant. Across these entangled relationships, human and GenAI agents are differentiated in ways that foreground the figure of a ghostly GenAI native speaker, experienced as competent, efficient, and self(‐)less. By contrast, learners' weaknesses are brought forth as deficient, slow, and unreliable. As our analysis reveals, the ghostly GenAI native speaker is rendered possible and intelligible through a range of existing apparatuses, whose enactment has summoned a dark energy, reconfiguring the way in which native‐speakerism exerts influence upon language learners—it reinforces a technical view of L2 writing and excludes learners not from native‐speaker communities but potentially from the sociality of L2 writing as a whole, with foreclosed possibilities for imagining diverse ways of relating to the target language.

items.title: THE IMPACT OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE ON THE TEACHING PROCESS IN HIGHER EDUCATION
items.abstract: The rapid rise of artificial intelligence (AI), especially generative AI, is transforming how higher-education institutions design instruction, support learners, evaluate knowledge, and structure academic work. In this paper, we review the implications of AI for teaching in universities, drawing upon contemporary scholarship, international guidance and select technical studies of service-oriented architectures, process modeling, database design and graph-based analytics. We performed a structured narrative review guided by a priori concepts of AI-supported personalization, tutoring, assessment, educator workload, academic integrity, privacy, bias and institutional governance. Evidence suggests that artificial intelligence can help improve access to timely feedback, adaptive support, course design and reduce routine workload. But access to a general-purpose model does not necessarily produce learning: benefits depend on pedagogical scaffolding, course alignment, verification, and ongoing supervision by humans. The key risks are: generated or biased outputs, cognitive offloading, unequal access, opaque data practices, and unreliable authorship judgments. The paper concludes that AI should be deployed as an augmentative educational infrastructure, not as a replacement for teachers. To ensure that technological efficiency benefits real learning and academic principles, universities need to combine AI literacy, redesigned assessment, privacy-by-design, transparent policies, interoperable systems, and ongoing assessment.

items.abstract: This research is based on evaluating the quality of AI-supported machine translation compared to human translation, in light of the rapid development of modern linguistic technologies. The significance of this study stems from the increasing role of machine translation across various media, cultural, and educational institutions, which makes it necessary to analyze its ability to produce linguistically and semantically accurate texts, the research problem revolves around the question: To what extent can artificial intelligence achieve translation quality comparable to that of human translators? And what are its limits in handling the diverse cultural and semantic contexts of texts? The study adopts a descriptive–analytical method, using a systematic comparison between human translations and machine translations. The sample included media, scientific, and literary texts, which were analyzed based on linguistic accuracy, contextual consistency, style, and the ability to translate specialized content The results indicate that modern machine translation systems based on neural networks exhibit high linguistic accuracy and good ability to maintain textual coherence, in addition to a notable advantage in speed and output volume compared to human translators. However, the study notes limitations in handling metaphors, dialects, precise technical terminology, and rhetorical structures with deep cultural Nuance the findings also confirm that human revision remains essential to ensure final quality, especially in sensitive fields. The study further shows that integrating artificial intelligence with human translators constitutes the most effective model for producing accurate and professional.

items.abstract: AbstractA central problem in classical metaphysics and rational theology is reconciling how a finite, created spirit—whether angelic or human—can receive, resonate with, and host an absolutely simple, uncompounded Divine Act (Actus Purus, Summa Theologiae I, q. 3) without violating the boundary conditions of either entity. Building upon the overarching Fractal Soul methodology, this paper demonstrates that all created spirits—both disembodied angelic substances and incarnate human souls—must operate with a nested, self-similar (fractal) topology. This structural architecture is the necessary created condition (ex parte creaturae) for resonant union with Divine Simplicity.However, while the fundamental ontological requirement for self-sacrificial kenotic hollowing is universal to all spirits as an analogical reflection of intra-Trinitarian perichoresis, the mode and temporal execution of this surrender diverge fundamentally based on hylomorphic constraints. For pure angelic spirits, the self-sacrificial choice for uncreated grace is total, immediate, and non-recursive (n = 1). Rooted in Patristic and Scotistic tradition, this angelic trial was an instantaneous test of Christological humility—a binary decision to bow before the revealed decree of the Incarnate Logos (Heb 1:6). Because angels lack matter and must forge their interior capacity through this all-encompassing act of self-sacrificing will to hollow their own unique Menger sponge faculties, this unrepeatable choice n = 1 instantiation provides the topological foundation for the Thomistic principle that every angel constitutes its own unique species (ST I, q. 50, a. 4). Finally, in accordance with Christ's teaching on the resurrection (isaggelloi, Luke 20:36), this temporal human recursion ultimately matures into an eternal, fixed likeness to the angelic state once hylomorphic friction is permanently resolved in glory. items.title: The Law of Geodesic Flow and the Conservation of Agency: Codifying the D.U.M.B.R.O.T. Pathology across Socio-Technical, Biomechanical, and Neurological Architectures
items.abstract: This monograph formalizes The Law of Geodesic Flow, a fundamental thermodynamic and differential-geometric principle dictating that directed force exerted in defiance of unconditioned boundary constraints dissipates entirely into localized entropy rather than kinematic displacement. Through a rigorous variational framework grounded in the Principle of Stationary Action and Noether's conservation theorems, we demonstrate that structural progress requires conformal alignment along the field’s geodesic trajectories. Extending this physical law to human-machine interaction, we introduce the Conservation of Agency Theorem: operational friction cannot be eliminated from a system; it can only be transferred. When cognitive and sensorimotor boundary negotiations are fully delegated to autonomous systems (such as end-to-end autonomous driving), the biological host undergoes D.U.M.B.R.O.T. (Downregulated User Motor Baseline via Reactive Optical Truncation). We provide an exhaustive neuro-ergonomic audit detailing how total algorithmic offloading induces prefrontal-striatal hypometabolism, hippocampal spatial map thinning, and visual saccadic decay. To illustrate scale-invariance, the doctrine is validated across three disparate empirical case studies: Thermodynamic Extraction Under Extreme Constraint: Non-allium, zero-ethanol Maillard synthesis within strict Jain-Halal nutritional parameters. Sartorial Ergonomics and Proportional Interference: Forensic structural vector analysis within contemporary Harlem street aesthetics. Automated Transit and Sensorimotor Decay: Neurological decoupling under Level 4/5 autonomous navigation systems. The work concludes with a comprehensive remediation protocol, detailing the kinetic, ocular, and institutional counter-measures necessary to preserve biological agency and baseline cognitive reserves in an increasingly automated socio-technical landscape.
